Oliver / Sasha — attaching the initial switchover checklist (PDF) and a client-snippets tarball. Below are the concrete implementation notes and sample code. This is intended to be pasted into your existing backend repo as a feature-flagged rollout.

High level rollout (recommended):
1) Sandbox validation (2 days): configure dev API key, validate token flows, run 10k token smoke tests.
2) Staged canary (30 min): route 2% of traffic to Redwood in a single region. Monitor error rate & latency.
3) Ramp (6h): 2% -> 25% -> 75% -> 100% with monitoring gates.
4) Rollback: DNS revert + rate-limit throttle to previous vendor for 15 minutes.

Endpoint differences and migration notes:
- Current vendor: POST https://api.legacy.ai/v1/stream
- Redwood primary: POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat/stream
- For session continuity: pass session_id in metadata. On canary, Redwood will accept the same session_id and warm KV cache on first few tokens; we recommend a brief grace period where both vendors accept incoming user messages.

Client-side timeouts / retry policy (recommended):
- Connect timeout: 3000 ms
- Read timeout (per-chunk): 30s
- Overall request deadline: 120s for full generation (tunable based on model and max tokens)

Retry matrix (simplified):
- 429 (rate limit): exponential backoff with full-jitter, initial delay 250 ms, max retries 5. If you see repeated 429s for specific user session, throttle that session locally (token quota per user).
- 5xx (server errors): immediate retry for idempotent endpoints only (e.g., embeddings). For streaming chat, do not auto-retry — surface a client error and allow user to retry.
- 408/504 (timeouts): retry with backoff, up to 3 attempts for idempotent calls.

Sample Node snippet (pseudo-code):
const fetchWithBackoff = async (url, opts) => {
  let attempt = 0;
  while (attempt < 5) {
    try {
      const res = await fetch(url, opts);
      if (res.status === 429) throw { type: 'rate_limit' };
      if (res.status >= 500) throw { type: 'server' };
      return res;
    } catch (e) {
      attempt++;
      const delay = Math.min(2000 * Math.pow(2, attempt), 10000) * Math.random(); // full jitter
      await new Promise(r => setTimeout(r, delay));
    }
  }
  throw new Error('max retries exceeded');
};

Go sample (pseudo-code):
// Use context with deadline for overall request
ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), 120*time.Second)
defer cancel()
req, _ := http.NewRequestWithContext(ctx, "POST", url, body)
client := &http.Client{Timeout: 30 * time.Second} // per-chunk read timeout handled at lower layer
resp, err := client.Do(req)

Operational notes:
- Token billing: Redwood tokens billed per-response; include metrics tags in requests (x-redwood-app-id) so Cost dashboards map to your internal teams.
- Rate-limit headers: Redwood returns X-RateLimit-Limit and X-RateLimit-Remaining; instrument your clients to lower concurrency when Remaining < 20%.

Attachments: integration-switchover-checklist.pdf, client-snippets.tar.gz

Hi Sasha — quick answers and a proposed warmup sequence below. I’ve attached a 1-page runbook section to the checklist (included in the PDF).

1) KV cache warmup sequence for session cutover:
  a) On first request with session_id on Redwood, accept the message and immediately return a short 202-ACCEPTED with a hint header X-RW-WARMUP: true if warmup required.
  b) In parallel, perform a low-cost prefix run to populate the KV cache for the session (first 1-2 tokens).
  c) Subsequent requests for the session are handled normally; if client sees X-RW-WARMUP: true, it should show a short typing indicator to users (under 800ms).
  d) If warmup fails due to transient errors, fallback to proxying to legacy vendor for that session for up to 2 minutes.

2) Per-merchant throttles: yes — Redwood supports per-api-key and per-customer quotas. Pass merchant_id in the metadata header (x-merchant-id) and we’ll enforce/apply throttles. We recommend 95th percentile traffic shaping in your gateway to avoid hitting hard limits.

3) Observability recommendations (span tags):
  - rw.session_id
  - rw.kv_warmup (bool)
  - rw.first_token_latency_ms
  - rw.model_variant
  - rw.rate_limit_remaining

Implementation runbook highlights (from attached checklist):
- Pre-cutover: verify account quota, verify api key scopes, run 10k token soak test.
- Canaries: export immediate metrics (error rate, p50/p95 latency, rate_limit_remaining).
- Post-cutover: 24h watch with on-call CS + SRE.

Next actions:
- Monica to schedule a 30-min spike session with your SREs this week.
- Oliver to confirm cutover start time (Nov 18 preferred).
- Irene to provide escalation list and on-call rotation.
